q1.explanationZh: 男孩本来想做鲨鱼，后来看了关于雄企鹅照顾幼崽的电视节目，决定以企鹅为题（decided to go for that as my topic）。C 鲨鱼是女孩找的照片；A 蚊子是他以为女孩选的题目。

q2.explanationZh: 男孩问是不是在 Forsyth Hotel，女孩说“就是体育中心旁边那家，没错”，所以哥哥在酒店工作。A 美术馆没回复他；B 体育中心只是酒店旁边的地方。

q3.explanationZh: 男孩要先放东西，建议在更衣室外面见（just outside the locker rooms），女孩说 Good idea。B 他说不是游泳池旁的那间；C 见面后再一起走去跑道。

q4.explanationZh: 台灯太贵没买；女孩包里的东西“有很宽的条纹”，还能配短裤，所以买的是条纹 T 恤。B 杂志只是她见过台灯的地方；C 台灯她明天才去找。

q5.explanationZh: 妈妈说可以坐环城巴士、随时上下车，男孩说自己选路线不错，就这么办（Let’s do that）。A、C 骑车和步行他们在家随时都能做，不是在这座城市里。

q6.explanationZh: 玻璃碗被他接住了没摔坏，但他的手肘碰到了水壶，水壶摔碎了（the jug … ended up on the floor in pieces）。A 碗没坏；B 玻璃杯只是和水壶配套的，没有提到被打碎。

q7.explanationZh: 女孩说网上有订票页面，座位图在电脑屏幕上看得更清楚；爸爸虽然更想去学校前台买，但说有问题会问她，即会在网上用电脑订。B 他最后没去前台；C 女孩说打电话很难打通。

q8.explanationZh: 男孩说从一开始就能猜到会发生什么，女孩说“我也是（So could I）”，两人都觉得结局很明显。B 男孩说不是演员的问题，还认为女儿一角演得很好；C 只有女孩觉得故事不真实，男孩不同意。

q9.explanationZh: 男孩说排长队、冲浪池太挤用不了，并提醒女孩去之前最好查查要等多久，这是在提醒她注意一个问题。A 他没有鼓励她去；C 经理压力大但答应改进，他没有抱怨她。

q10.explanationZh: 女孩说要学的很多，但她不着急，宁愿慢慢学好（I’m in no hurry），对自己的进度很放松。A 她说不确定手的位置，并不自信；C 她说有观众不会让她紧张，紧张的是男孩。

q11.explanationZh: 椅子没坏，只是太大；姐姐建议不要书桌，他想留着，最后说可以把东西挪一挪（move things around a bit），即改变家具位置。A 他不想减少家具；B 椅子没有坏。

q12.explanationZh: 男孩问这些到底有什么意义（What was the actual point of it all），女孩解释是为了了解植物如何生长，两人在讨论切花的目的。A 只有男孩抱怨；B 只有女孩觉得有趣。

q13.explanationZh: 男孩说船上有很多复杂的名称，要记的东西太多，不确定自己能不能记住（There’ll be a lot to remember），担心会忘。A 他说身体好没问题；B 舅舅说会让他自己驾船。

q14.explanationZh: Ben 说最好的羊每天产约 5 升奶，但更常见的是约 4 升（more usual … around 4 litres），题目问“典型的”羊，所以填 4；3 升是最低量。

q15.explanationZh: 青贮饲料的主要原料是草，而且是农场自己种的（we actually grow it here）；玉米是买来的，不是农场种的。

q16.explanationZh: Ben 挤完奶、喂完羊后，儿子来帮忙，负责大量的清洁工作（There’s loads of cleaning to do, and he takes care of that）。

q17.explanationZh: Ben 上午大部分时间忙着算账，所以待在办公室（office）里；他更想去田里或羊舍，但实际上没有。

q18.explanationZh: 兽医每两周（once a fortnight = every two weeks）来一次检查羊的健康；邻居和学生没有说每两周来。

q19.explanationZh: 网站是 www.cormack.uk，Ben 逐个字母拼出了 C-O-R-M-A-C-K。

q20.explanationZh: Jenny 说父母为她做了很多：叫她起床、送她去体育中心再送她上学，说明她很感激父母。A 她一醒来就想滑冰，不讨厌早起；C 她说错过课不好，从不迟到。

q21.explanationZh: Jenny 说教练总是认真听，并询问她的意见（pays attention and asks me for my opinions），这是她喜欢的。A 没说他讲得慢；B 教练知道什么时候该休息，并不是逼她苦练。

q22.explanationZh: Jenny 说奖品不是最重要的，比赛时一心想着赢会让她无法专注表演，所以她不去想奖品。A 她没说要参加更多比赛；C 她有时得第二名反而滑得更好，赢不能证明能力。

q23.explanationZh: Jenny 说看录像让她想马上回到冰上，再做一遍、做得更好（get straight back on the ice to try and do it better），即渴望再次表演。B 她没说对进步印象深刻；C 她没说因错误而生气。

q24.explanationZh: Jenny 说正确地摔倒是滑冰者必须学的技巧之一（one of the techniques skaters need to learn），是滑冰必不可少的一部分。A 她不担心摔倒；B 她只说学会摔法会少疼，没说不像别人想的那么疼。

q25.explanationZh: Jenny 说要提高体能，打算多去健身房和跑步，即加强锻炼计划。B 出国看看要以后再说；C 她只说不减少上冰时间，没说要增加。

content.v: Test One. There are four parts to the test. You will hear each part twice. We will now stop for a moment. Please ask any questions now, because you must not speak during the test.
Now look at the instructions for Part One.
For each question, choose the correct answer. Look at question one.
One. What is the boy’s biology project about?
Hey! Just look at these amazing photos I’ve found for my biology project.

Wow, sharks! There are so many different species, aren’t there? I thought about doing my project on them, too. But then I saw this programme on TV last week. It was all about how male penguins look after their babies in freezing temperatures. I became so interested that I decided to go for that as my topic. I thought you’d chosen mosquitos?
Yeah, but then I changed my mind.
Two. Where is the girl’s older brother working?
I know your older brother was really interested in working at the new art gallery in town. Did he get a job there?
Well, he did write to them actually, but they never replied. So, he’s found a job somewhere else.
Where? At the Forsyth Hotel? I saw him going in there the other day.
The one near the sports centre. That’s right.
With that sculpture of the two lions at the entrance. I know it cos I often pass it – me and my cousin play football at the sports centre.
Three. Where will the boy and girl meet?
Hi, how are you doing? Are you still going to the sports club after school?
Sure … Shall we meet at the running track as usual?

Well, I’d definitely like to start with a run, but I’ll need to put my stuff somewhere first. So how about meeting just outside the locker rooms? Not the ones by the swimming pool, the other ones. Then we can walk over to the running track together.
Good idea. Shall we say half past four?
Yeah – great. See you later.
Four. What did the girl buy yesterday?
How was your shopping trip with Mum yesterday? Did you get a lamp for your bedroom?
There was a beautiful purple one I liked, but it was too expensive. It’s a shame because it was just like one I saw in a magazine the other day.
What’s in the bag then?
Look. Isn’t it fantastic?
It’s certainly got big stripes! I’m not sure it’ll look right on you.
I think it’ll be great with my shorts. I’m going to try and find a lamp tomorrow – you could come along.
Five. How will the mother and her son explore the city?
How are we going to explore the city when we get there, Mum?
It says in the guidebook we can join a walking tour. There are also cycle tours, which look fun.
Sounds interesting. Are those both group tours?
Yes, with a guide. If we’d prefer to be more independent, there’s a bus that goes round the city. We can get on and off wherever we like.
Choosing our own route sounds good. Let’s do that. We can walk or cycle any time we like at home.
OK then.
Six. What did the boy break?
What was that noise I heard earlier? It sounded like something got broken. Is everything OK?

Yes, I’m really sorry, Mum, I was in the kitchen and I knocked a glass bowl off the shelf. I managed to catch it in time, so it’s not damaged but, while I was reaching out for it, my elbow hit the jug and it ended up on the floor in pieces!
The one that came with that lovely set of glasses? That’s a shame. Oh well, accidents happen! As long as you’re OK.
Seven. How will the girl’s father book tickets for the school show?
Dad, will you book the tickets for the school show today?
How do we buy them?

You have to do it from home to avoid queues of people buying tickets at school. There’s a booking page on the school website, or you can phone. I’ve heard it’s hard to get an answer though if you call. Also, there’s a plan of the seats online, which is far clearer on a computer screen.
I’d rather just get them at the school reception, but never mind, I’ll ask you if I have a problem.
That is the end of Part One.
Now look at Part Two. For each question, choose the correct answer.
Eight. You will hear a boy and a girl talking about a film.
I found that film disappointing. It wasn’t the fault of the actors, either.
I wasn’t that impressed. I didn’t think they had the right person to play the pilot. The actress playing the daughter wasn’t too bad, though.
One of the strongest performances I thought. My problem was that right from the beginning you could predict what would happen.
So could I. I knew everything’d be OK, and I was right. But I just couldn’t believe in the story. What pilot would attempt to take off in a snowstorm?
Come on! He had no choice – he had to get home!
Nine. You will hear a boy talking to a girl about a water sports centre.
Hi, there. I went to the new water sports centre yesterday – it’s got a huge swimming pool. It looks great.
I heard it’s got a special pool for surfing, too.

That’s right. The thing is, so many people have heard about it, there were long queues to get into the building. And then, we couldn’t use the surfing pool because it was so crowded. Dad talked to the manager. She was very stressed, but promised to try and make waiting times shorter in future. If you’re thinking of going there, you’d better check how long you’ll have to wait.
OK, thanks.
Ten. You will hear two friends talking about playing the piano.
How are your piano lessons going?

Not too bad. There’s a lot to learn, but I’m in no hurry. I’d rather go slowly and try to learn everything well. But I don’t think I’ll ever be completely sure about the correct position for my hands.
Everyone feels like that at first. You’re playing in the school show at the end of term, aren’t you?
That’s right. Only a short thing, though. Aren’t you playing, too?
Yes, I’m a bit worried about performing in front of so many people, actually.
Oh, that doesn’t bother me – you know, having an audience.
Eleven. You will hear a boy telling his sister about plans for his room.
I’m going to ask Mum for a new chair for my room.
What’s wrong with the one you’ve got?
It’s not broken or anything, but it’s far too big now I’ve got that new desk. There’s hardly enough space to walk between the chair and the bed.
Do you really need the desk? You do most of your homework in the living room anyway.
It’s got all my stuff on it now, so I’m keen to keep it. I suppose I could move things around a bit. That might work. Will you give me a hand?
No problem.
Twelve. You will hear two students talking about a science lesson.
That science lesson was a bit different, wasn’t it?
But why do we need to learn about different parts of flowers? It’s not that useful.
I think it’s really interesting …
The flowers were so small it was difficult to cut them open.
I know – but that was so we could see what they were like inside. I found it fun.
At least, we could ask our teacher for help.
And I did several times.
What was the actual point of it all, though?
Well, it was so we could understand how plants work. Weren’t you listening?
Yeah, I just wasn’t sure!
Thirteen. You will hear a boy telling his friend about going sailing.
What are you doing at the weekend?
My uncle’s going to teach me to sail his boat.
Do you have to be fit for that?

Yes, really fit, but that’s no problem for me! My uncle’s going to show me what to do. There are loads of complicated names and the ropes are all for different things. There’ll be a lot to remember. I’m not sure I’ll manage! I’ll need plenty of practice, but he said I’ll have a chance to sail the boat myself for a bit, you know, be in charge of the whole thing.
That is the end of Part Two.
Now look at Part Three.
For each question, write the correct answer in the gap. Write one or two words or a number or a date or a time. Look at questions 14 to 19 now. You have 20 seconds.
You will hear a talk at a school by a goat farmer called Ben Jones.

Hello, I’m Ben Jones. I run a goat farm where my goats produce delicious, fresh milk. I’d like to tell you something about life on the farm. My day starts early. I get up at 5:30 a.m. and I go down to the part of the farm where the goats sleep. I’ve got 30 goats and a really good one produces around 5 litres of milk per day. But it’s more usual to get around 4 litres. The lowest I’d expect would be 3 litres. After milking the goats, it’s feeding time. Goats will eat almost anything, but on my farm, we give them something called ‘silage’. The main ingredient is grass – we actually grow it here on the farm. We also add corn to it, but I buy that. My 18-year-old son joins me after I’ve done the milking and feeding. There’s loads of cleaning to do, and he takes care of that. While he’s busy, I go inside to help with preparing breakfast for the family. For most of the morning, I’m busy with my accounts – it’s amazing how much there is to do, so that’s why I spend lots of time in my office. Actually, I’d prefer to spend more time in the fields or in the farm buildings with the goats. The farm has regular visitors. My neighbours love to stop and watch the goats in the fields. One of them’s a student who wants to be a farmer, too. The vet comes round once a fortnight to check the goats are healthy. In the evening, after a final look at the goats, we’re all in bed very early. If you want to learn more about the farm, look at our website which is www dot cormack dot uk. That’s C-O-R-M-A-C-K – or, even better, come and visit us!
That is the end of Part Three.
Now look at Part Four. For each question, choose the correct answer.
Look at questions 20 to 25 now. You have 45 seconds.
You will hear an interview with a girl called Jenny Baker, who is a young ice skater.
Today I’m interviewing Jenny Baker, a young ice skater.
Hi.
So, Jenny, do you have to do a lot of training as an ice skater?

Of course. Just like any other sport, practice is essential, and, for me, that means getting up early every day. As soon as I’m awake, all I want to do is skate. My parents do so much for me, waking me up and taking me to the sports centre, and then school every morning. I’ve never been late for school. It wouldn’t be a good idea to miss a class.
And do you have your own ice skating coach?

Yes, I do. I’m so lucky. He gives me excellent advice and has lots of different ways of showing me how to do things on the ice. Another positive thing is he always pays attention and asks me for my opinions. And he knows when it’s time to relax and have a break, which is good!
Do you ice skate in competitions?

Yes, I’ve entered quite a few of them. I only skate because I love it, though. It’s funny, sometimes when I come second, I think I’ve skated better than when I’ve come first. A prize is nice, but not the most important thing. I find focusing on winning when I’m skating prevents me from concentrating on my performance.
Do you ever watch your skating performances?

We record them all on video. Watching them’s a great way to improve. At first, I couldn’t see what I was doing wrong, but I’m learning to notice the details. Watching my performances makes me want to get straight back on the ice to try and do it better.
Do you often fall over on the ice?

All the time! Doing it properly’s just one of the techniques skaters need to learn. If you’re not prepared to fall, you won’t attempt new things and, when you do, it’ll be more painful. It hurts less when you know how to do it. You just pick yourself up and try to look as if it hasn’t bothered you.
What are your future plans?

To keep skating! But also to keep improving. To do that, I need to build my fitness. Going to the gym and running are great ways to get stronger, so I plan to do things like that more without reducing my time on the ice. I’d like to travel more and see how ice skaters in other countries do things, but that’ll have to wait.
Thanks, Jenny … [fade]
That is the end of Part Four.
You now have six minutes to write your answers on the answer sheet.
You have one more minute.
That is the end of the test.
